newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Momentum to hike year earnings.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Momentum to hike year earnings.

text.p: Momentum Life Assurers Ltd would post robust growth in annual earnings buoyed by contributions from its subsidiaries and growth in assets under management, analysts said on Friday.
Momentum is due to report results for the year ended June 30 on Sunday.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings rising by between 25 and 30 percent to between 91.0 and 95.0 cents a share with a consensus 92.3 cents. They expected a dividend of 50.7 cents a share, rising from 40.5 cents last year.

Analysts said a turnaround in Momentum's health division and in Aegis Insurance Company Ltd would lift profits. Earnings would be further boosted by a 35 percent increase in wholly-owned subsidiary RMB Holdings Ltd's attributable earnings for the year to end-June.
Assets under management had grown during the year and stood at roughly 30 billion rand, said David Southey, an analyst at Edey Rogers.
"(If) you work it out on an average of 0.2 percent commission on that (30 billion rand) you have about 60 million rand from that source," Southey said.
He said Momentum's share price had firmed in anticipation of the rosy results. On Friday shares were untraded at 35.80 rand after touching a year best of 36 rand on Thursday.
"It (the share price) has really been racing ahead. They are very expensive but the performance is there," Southey said.
